column1: # Claude's two passes for Imagination Nights in Spanish (Mindset door). 'pastor' = the safety and ethics read for this door (no faith words or links, no scripture in any wording, no outcome or health promises, no controlling other people, real help pointed to); 'cultural' = the native-Spanish listener read.

column3: Same safety shape as the English set, in our own words: each teaching says plainly it is imagination and feeling, not a promise, and that the daytime steps stay real; the love night never pictures another person changing their mind and points anyone in a frightening relationship to help; revision keeps owed apologies real; the work night pictures a bill paid on time, not riches. No faith words, no verse in any wording (scripture_woven false), no teacher named.
column5: Written for Spanish speakers, not translated line by line: tú throughout, Latin American usage (cobijas, recámara, apagador, trastes, carro, plática), natural turns (quedarse con las ganas, hacerse de la vista gorda, un ajetreo del bueno); no adjective assumes the listener's gender (sentado o sentada, despierto, acostado rewritten); no vosotros, no English; accents and ñ checked; 18.9-20.0 min by the gate's pacing.

column3: Our own words, no faith words or scripture; each teaching names imagination, not a promise. Self-worth night gives 988 and says it answers in Spanish; old-memory revision tells listeners not to use abuse or trauma memories and to seek a trained person; evening walk makes no health promise and offers a wheelchair or porch version; family night never forces anyone to change; business night pictures enough, not riches, and says to get good advice.
column5: Ordinary, dignified scenes rewritten for a Latin American listener (domingo por la tarde y la sobremesa, el pueblo de los abuelos, techos de teja, una banca o una barda, la colonia, la tiendita y el puesto de comida); warm and plain; no gendered listener adjectives; 19.1-20.0 min.

column3: Our own words, no faith words or scripture; every teaching says imagination, not a promise, and keeps daytime work real. Quiet-house, hard-talk and kind-no nights point anyone afraid of someone to a trained person; friendship and hard-talk nights never picture making another person agree; money night pictures bills covered and a little saved, with advice from someone who knows; rest night makes no sleep claim; the porch night thanks one's life, not a deity.
column5: Natural Spanish (los números cuadran, me alcanza, una palomita en la lista, darle la vuelta a la manzana, tomates o chiles en el huerto, una noche de micrófono abierto, palomillas en la luz del porche); the kind-no night speaks of women in the third person so the narrator claims no life of its own; no gendered listener adjectives; no em dashes or exclamation marks; 18.8-20.0 min.
